newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, Israel to proceed on interim peace issues.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Israel to proceed on interim peace issues.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Monday work with the PLO on outstanding interim peace deal issues could resume in earnest now that the Palestinians had pledged to act on security matters.

But Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) negotiator Nabil Shaath, speaking to reporters alongside Levy after the two held talks in Jerusalem on Sunday, said a deadlock on proceeding with final peace talks remained.

"We decided that the committees will resume their work," Levy said, referring to talks on future Palestinian air and sea ports, a "safe passage" between the Gaza Strip and West Bank, and Palestinian prisoners held by Israel.
A PLO official speaking on condition he not be named told Reuters talks on those matters had been underway for sometime but had not been progressing.
Shaath told reporters Levy's attitude on the interim issues contributed to "confidence building measures" and said those steps "indicate the desire to go to the second phase".
But he added: "I know that the issues upon which this deadlock developed still await solution: the issues of settlement, Jerusalem, and the return to (final) negotiations".

Relations between Israel and the Palestinians plunged in crisis over Israel's breaking ground in March on Har Homa Jewish settlement on a hilltop known to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim on the edge of East Jerusalem.
The PLO has vowed it will not resume substantive negotiations until Israel halts settlement.

Palestinian anger over Jewish settlement building was fuelled last week when Israel's Jerusalem municipality granted a permit for an American Jewish businessman to build some 70 homes for Jews in Ras al-Amoud Arab neighbourhood.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to block that building plan "at this time" but refused to stop the Har Homa settlement.

On Monday, Israel's Interior Ministry said construction on the Ras al-Amoud enclave could not be launched until an appeal filed against the plan by two left-wing Jerusalem city council members was heard next month.
Jerusalem is the thorniest issue between Israel and the PLO.
Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and says it will never give up an inch of what it calls its "eternal, united" capital.
The Palestinians want East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state and say building for Jews there pre-empts final peace talks.
Under interim peace deals, the first in 1993, Israel has handed most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank to PLO rule.
